design.contract: D2: the smaller change is an empty package list, not a new kind field: no new field, no column, no migration. IntakeConfirmSchema drops min(1) on packages and refuses a body naming neither a package nor a target; every body that was valid before parses and digests unchanged.
design.storage: usp_intake_confirmations requires 1 to 100 stored packages (database/sql/95-ingestion/intake-targets.sql, not this task's path). A cards-only confirmation therefore stores, for each package of its targets, the pin exactly as the confirmation that recorded it named it (revision + 1 equals the package's committed revision). Counts, findings, retry and the run's per-target revision check then work unchanged.
design.marker: The stored reason states the kind: 'Confirmed by the officer in intake confirmation <id> on <day> to card buildings already recorded.' isCardsOnly() compares the stored reason with that exact sentence for the row's own id and time; Progress already shows the reason.
design.checks: A cards-only target must be in the case, of a COMMITTED package an earlier confirmation of this case recorded, at readiness recorded and listed in no confirmation; otherwise 409 INTAKE_CONFIRMATION_STALE with the reason in words. Its readiness stays recorded; it takes the confirmation id and the words 'Listed for a card; it is carded in the order listed.'
design.run: D1: the confirmation's commit job sees the marker and skips the commit loop; it carries each listed target through the existing carry steps (snapshot, identity, plan, plan confirmation, packet, card, verify) in the stored order and renews the lease after each. A refusal stops that building in its own words and the others continue; the job then fails with the first refusal's code, as a refused package does. A lost lease stops nothing; the next attempt skips carded and stopped targets and each step whose artefact is stored.
design.studio: D3: once a batch has a recorded package and recorded buildings, the run panel on the batch page shows '<n> recorded buildings have no card yet.' and 'Make cards for the next 100'. It reads the recorded target pages in stored order and keeps the first 100 that no confirmation lists, then opens the existing confirmation panel listing them with what will be made; the officer types the acknowledgement and presses 'Make these cards'.
design.tidy: D5: the RECIPE_APPROVAL message in service.ts uses a plain ASCII apostrophe in file's.

gaps: No runtime walk: a cards-only confirmation of 100 Niagara buildings on a live box is still needed to show the cards are made and the lease is held.
The kind is marked by the stored reason sentence because the table forbids an empty package list; a kind column would need a migration in database/sql, outside this task.

A building opened while a cards-only run works does not jump its queue: the run carries its list in order inside one job, and the priority order applies to target jobs only. A retry of a stopped cards-only building goes through the existing target job and so is prioritised as before.

The count line uses counts.recorded, which also holds recorded buildings already listed and waiting for their card; the action lists only the ones no confirmation names. If every such building is listed, the panel says so and the press stays disabled.
